h1: 76 of 100 apps could become agent toolkits today. Half of the rest are held back by a price, not a partner.
lede: An agent built on Composio's own search and fetch tools researched 100 apps for auth, access gate, API surface, MCP and buildability. It cited a source URL and a verbatim quote for every answer. Five verification loops then flagged 68 apps, changed answers on 43 and sent 22 to a human. On a hand-checked sample, accuracy rose from 75.8% after one pass to 81.1% after the loops.

patterns.title: apps can be built today with free, self-serve credentials
patterns.body: All 10 communications apps are open. Support & Helpdesk and Marketing are the least open, at 6 of 10 each. Pass 1 said 81; the loops moved apps out of 'build now' when they found trials, paid plans and review gates.

patterns.title: The most common blocker is a paid plan or a trial, not a partnership
patterns.body: Zendesk, Datadog, Snowflake, Smartsheet, Ahrefs, Grain and six others need a paid tier or stop working after a trial. A funded test account unlocks these without a negotiation. Only 6 need a partner or enterprise contract (DealCloud, PitchBook, LinkedIn Ads, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Ramp, Otter AI), and 4 need an app review (Google Ads, Amazon SP-API, Gorgias, Pinterest).

patterns.title: apps use OAuth 2, and most of them also offer a static key
patterns.body: OAuth 2 is the main method for 56 apps. 78 apps document two or more methods, usually OAuth for acting on behalf of many users plus an API key or personal token for a single account. So most toolkits need two auth configs, not one.

patterns.title: vendors already publish their own MCP server
patterns.body: Pass 1 found 54. The MCP probe loop found most of the rest, which a single search had missed. Ecommerce lags (4 of 10). The agent's MCP labels were right on 17 of 19 sample apps.

patterns.title: build-now apps have no toolkit page on docs.composio.dev
patterns.body: WooCommerce, BigCommerce, Magento, Ecwid, MongoDB Atlas, Vonage, Lark, Podio, SE Ranking, Binance and Threads: the obvious toolkit URL returns 404. These are the quickest additions. Check each first: Composio's own /toolkits API also left out 7 apps that do have pages (Twilio, Aircall, Gladly and others), and the agent missed that Threads needs Meta app review.

patterns.title: apps need outreach, and they cluster in ads, enterprise data and fintech
patterns.body: Ads platforms gate on app review (Google Ads, LinkedIn Ads). Enterprise data vendors sell access by contract (DealCloud, PitchBook). Marketplaces and fintech require approval (Amazon SP-API, Ramp). These are the conversations to start early.

acc_intro: Twenty apps, two per category from a seeded random draw, were labelled from vendor docs and checked by hand. iPayX could not be confirmed, which leaves 19 apps × 5 fields = 95 judgements. The same 95 are scored for pass 1 and pass 2.
misses: Gladly got worse because of the loops. Pass 1 correctly said enterprise-only. The verifier read 'sandbox environment' as free self-serve and the adjudicator agreed. The root cause is my rubric: it counted any free sandbox as self-serve without requiring that anyone can sign up.
Ecwid is still wrong. Its docs say 'Only stores on paid plans can access API'; the agent read the free custom-app flow as self-serve.
Threads is still marked build now. Public use needs Meta App Review.
Sherlock: the local-tool rule and the verifier both flagged 'build now', but the adjudicator kept it, so it sits in the human queue.
Harvest: the loops changed MCP to 'official' from a weak source, and called it trial-only although a free plan exists.
Amazon SP-API: the MCP probe did not find Amazon's own sp-api-dev-mcp in its samples repo.
Auth over-listing on 8 of 19 apps. The agent lists every method it sees mentioned, such as Basic for GitHub or OAuth for Plaid's bank-connection flow. It picks the right main method on 18 of 19.
limits: 19 scored apps give 95 judgements, so one answer moves the score by about a point.
The reference labels were drafted by Claude from vendor docs before the agent ran, then confirmed by Gaurav opening every source. That is a light human check, not two independent annotators.

Free tiers shaped the run. Gemini's stronger model ran out of quota, so every extraction used gemini-3.5-flash-lite. Groq's daily caps pushed the verifier across four models, one of them small (allam-2-7b). 7 apps got no blind verifier.

The rubric was not re-tuned on the sample's misses, because that would inflate the score. Next fixes: count a sandbox only if anyone can sign up for it, read the pricing page for trial-only or paid-only API access, and list only auth methods documented for the public API.
Access rules and pricing change often. Each answer's evidence URL records what the docs said on 24 Sep 2026.
human_notes: Chose the free LLM keys and created a Composio project key with tool-execution permission; restarted runs when free-tier caps hit.
30 fields on 22 apps ended in the review queue. They are tagged 'needs human' in the table rather than silently resolved.
